newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end easier, OTC stocks weak.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end easier, OTC stocks weak.

text.p: Singapore shares ended easier on Wednesday after a morning rally petered out. Dealers said sentiment turned in the afternoon session, especially for Malaysian issues traded over the counter.
"Liquidity is still not in the market. A lot of retail players are still wounded from their losses last week," said a dealer with a local firm.

She said funds had been nibbling at selected blue chips but volumes were not heavy as prices had not fallen much. However, electronic issues were still in demand and pushed the SES electronics index up 0.34 points to 101.98.

But the benchmark Straits Times Industrial Index ended off 1.51 points at 2,103.20 while the UOB OTC index closed 3.13 points lower at 1,223.34. Total market volume was 166.74 million shares with 185 losers beating 162 gainers.
Newly-listed Serial System ended at Singapore $0.61 against an initial offer price of S$0.58 with 4.5 million shares traded.
NatSteel climbed for a second day, rising to a new high of S$3.80, up six cents, on volume of 2.4 million shares. Gainers included Elec & Eltek, Venture Manufacturing and SIA foreign.
